chaining: A no-card platform in Lagos with 10 projects and 100 GB is a place to land an API service whose users are in West Africa, which is the one thing a European or American free tier cannot give: a short path to the audience, with the inference endpoint on the same host removing a second vendor from the chain.

limits.value: 100 GB of bandwidth a month across 10 projects is the whole allowance and the platform does not bill overage, so the service stops rather than charging, which makes an unexpected traffic spike a hard stop instead of an invoice.

notes: Africa's answer to the free-PaaS tier, and the first one that is free rather than a trial: a07-regional already records GoCloud (USD 300 credits, Lagos) and Savannaa (750 hours of t2.micro for 12 months) as trials, and this is the perpetual complement to both. Three more Nigerian and South African candidates were read and are thinner: Zanode (Cape Town) offers a card-free trial with 3 projects, one managed PostgreSQL and 10 GB of bandwidth, HostNowNow's sibling products bundle a free tier with the paid ones, and Ping Africa bills in KES from 500 a month with no free lane. Not established: the per-project memory and CPU cap on Flux Free, which the product page does not state.
